passages.text: The Heat Tax: How Temperature Slows Your Marathon. strong relationship. - The slope is approximately **1 minute slower per °F** of midday temperature. - Going from **50°F to 80°F** adds roughly **31 minutes** to the median finish time. **Why heat costs so much:** - Your body diverts blood flow to the skin for cooling, leaving less for working muscles. - Core temperature rises, heart rate drifts upward at the same pace, and dehydration compounds the effect. - The penalty grows nonlinearly as temperatures climb into the 70s and 80s °F.

passages.text: The Heat Tax: How Temperature Slows Your Marathon. Heat is one of the most powerful and predictable forces acting on marathon times, and it is easy to underestimate on race morning. **What 14 years of Boston data reveal (weather-paired):** - Per-year median finish time versus race-day midday temperature correlates at **r=0.86.** A very strong relationship. - The slope is approximately **1 minute slower per °F** of midday temperature. - Going from **50°F to 80°F** adds roughly **31 minutes** to the median finish time.
